description: Road-level reciprocity matrix for baseline, coordinate-corrected, and connectivity-repaired candidates
methodology: For each declared road link (elementType=road), check if a reverse-direction link of opposite type exists in the target road. Also check for same-direction reciprocals (one-way loops).

coordinate_corrected.note: identical to baseline — coordinate changes do not affect link structure

connectivity_repaired.note: New successor links (7144) have no corresponding predecessor links in target roads. Of 7144 new successor links: 1012 create reciprocal pairs with existing predecessor links (valid), 6132 point to roads where the reverse link would be predecessor (missing), creating directionally invalid state.

analysis.directionally_wrong_definition: A successor link A→B creates a directionally_wrong state if road B has a predecessor link to A but road A does not have a predecessor link to road B (or vice versa for predecessor links). This means the link is one-directional without matching reverse.
analysis.root_cause: Successor-only repairs: For each new successor link A→B, the repair algorithm should have also added a predecessor link B→A. Without the reverse link, the topology is asymmetric. The algorithm attempted predecessor repairs (4596 proposed) but accepted 0, then compensated by adding successsor-only links (7144), creating directional mismatches.
analysis.open_drive_travel_semantics: In OpenDRIVE, successor of road X maps to predecessor of road Y when X flows into Y. A bidirectional road connection requires X's successor=Y AND Y's predecessor=X. The repair algorithm violated this by adding only X's successor=Y without Y's predecessor=X.
